newsitem.title: USA: Campbell, Heinz in mediation on executive.
newsitem.headline: Campbell, Heinz in mediation on executive.

text.p: Mediation was due to begin Monday between Campbell Soup Co. and H.J. Heinz Co. in a dispute over Heinz's hiring of a top executive from the rival soup company, the companies said.
Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said Campbell had agreed to the mediation on the condition that the executive, Daniel O'Neill, did not work for Heinz for the duration of the mediation.
Campbell contends that O'Neill, the former head of Campbell's U.S. soup division, is bound by a non-competitive agreement and cannot work for Heinz.
"We have agreed to mediation, but we only agreed to it on the stipulation that (O'Neill) would not work there," Lowery said.
Heinz hired O'Neill to head its pet food and Star-Kist tuna operations, and O'Neill sued Campbell in Pennsylvania state court to release him from the agreement.
Campbell in turn sued in U.S. District Court in Camden, N.J., to block O'Neill from working for Heinz.
A hearing on Campbell's suit has been scheduled for Feb. 3, Lowery said.
